dedupe_keys.name: commercial building energy saver cbes with the deep database of energy efficiency performance

description: CBES is a Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory web tool for small and medium office and retail buildings in California that offers energy benchmarking and three levels of retrofit analysis. It has prototype models for seven building types, six vintages and 16 California climate zones and about 80 energy conservation measures for lighting, envelope, plug loads, HVAC and hot water. Its preliminary analysis draws on DEEP, the database of energy efficiency performance, compiled from about ten million EnergyPlus simulations run on the NERSC supercomputer, which lets owners screen hundreds of single and packaged measures without an audit; its detailed analysis calibrates a model and runs OpenStudio and EnergyPlus on demand. Coverage: California commercial buildings, with a national version called CBESPro. Access: free web tool with a login. Licence: terms not stated on the pages read. Caveats: DEEP was published in 2015 and covers prototype buildings, not measured ones. Simulation uses are rapid retrofit screening for building stocks, cooling load reduction for heat resilience and savings estimates for portfolio planning. Related records: EnergyPlus, OpenStudio, DOE prototype building models and CityBES.
